primitives.name: Fielding Limit Boundary
primitives.verbatim_quote: This particular hit he should regard as his limit, and anything inside of that he should consider it his bounden duty to take and field to first in time.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'d': 'distance in meters from home plate', 'T_{\\text{reach}}': 'time to reach ball in seconds', 'T_{\\text{handle}}': 'time to handle and throw in seconds'}
primitives.assumptions: Ball trajectory is linear; reaction time is constant; fielding area is planar.
primitives.breakdown_regime: $ T_{\text{reach}}(d) \geq T_{\text{handle}}(d) $ implies failure to field.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE state transition: $ \sigma_{\text{ball}} \rightarrow \sigma_{\text{field}} $, and to GSI probabilistic error model: $ P(\text{error} | d) $
layer2.telemetry: Distance threshold $ d_{\text{limit}} $ and reaction time $ T_{\text{react}} $

primitives.name: Narrow Fielding Range
primitives.verbatim_quote: Many amateur second basemen, otherwise excellent, take as their limit a much narrower field, and hence, while they do not make many errors, their opponents enjoy many little-deserved "safe" hits.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{\\text{amateur}}': 'radius of amateur fielding range in meters', 'R_{\\text{pro}}': 'radius of professional fielding range in meters'}
primitives.assumptions: Amateur players underestimate optimal fielding radius; opponent strategy exploits margin.
primitives.breakdown_regime: $ R_{\text{amateur}} < R_{\text{pro}} $ leads to suboptimal hit classification.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI risk-adjusted hit classification: $ \mathcal{C}_{\text{hit}}^{\text{safe}} = f(R_{\text{range}}, \theta_{\text{strategy}}) $
layer2.telemetry: Hit classification accuracy $ A_{\text{safe}} $ and range deviation $ \Delta R $

primitives.name: Underhand Throwing Practice
primitives.verbatim_quote: Throwing of every conceivable fashion is on this account permissible for a second baseman, and I have seen one of the best professional players almost scoop the ball, with one motion of his hand, from the ground into the first baseman's hands.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'v_{\\text{underhand}}': 'velocity of underhand throw in m/s', 't_{\\text{throw}}': 'time to execute throw in seconds'}
primitives.assumptions: Underhand throws are faster than overhand when executed from extended reach.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE motion planning kernel: $ \mathcal{T}_{\text{throw}} = g(\Delta x, v_{\text{underhand}}) $
layer2.telemetry: Throw execution time $ t_{\text{throw}} $ and distance from first base $ \Delta x $

The narrow fielding range primitive highlights a systemic bias in amateur players who define their operational limits too conservatively, leading to misclassification of safe hits. This introduces a strategic vulnerability in hit evaluation. Underhand throwing practice addresses kinematic constraints by optimizing motion efficiency under physical displacement, enabling timely throws even when body posture precludes overhand mechanics. These primitives form a coherent framework for modeling second baseman behavior in dynamic game states.
